subject: The three per-party recon slots: the whole of 008073C0 with its callees, the membership and detection rule behind the intrusive chain at slot+0DE8h, the rest of 00806B10 and what it writes into the nineteen Lua category tables, and what the three recon indices are.
reuses: include/bsp/fixed_step_countdown.hpp for kReconSlotSize, kReconSlotIndexOffset, kReconSlotDirtyOffset, kReconSlotArrayOffsets/Length/Stride and kReconSlotCount; include/bsp/recon_values.hpp for recon_category_names_00e0b590; docs/OBSERVER_LIFETIME.md names for 00694A60 and 006952A0; docs/ENTITY_CLASS_IDS.md for every class id; docs/UNIT_INSTANCE_LAYOUT.md for +54h, +5Ch..+60h, +C4h, +C8h, +170h, +174h, +1E4h

answer.question: (1) The membership rule: what decides that a unit appears in party P's recon list.
answer.result: Four independent conditions, none of which is a line-of-sight trace. (a) The unit's class id is one of the twenty-two 00805F60 pushes into the singleton vector 00806480 returns: 35h, 07h, 0Ah, 0Bh, 0Ch, 0Dh, 08h, 09h, 0Eh, 13h, 10h, 12h, 11h, 15h, 16h, 17h, 19h, 1Bh, 45h, 46h, 2Bh, 34h. The scan only ever walks the world registry's per-class list for these. (b) The unit passes the gate at 008074D5: +5Ch set, +5Dh clear, +60h clear, +5Eh clear, then vtable[5Ch](2), IsKindOf(02h). (c) 008065B0 buckets it by relation, a pure function of the slot's index at +28h and the unit's party at +54h: relation = (slotIndex == 2) ? (party == 2 ? own : neutral) : (slotIndex == party ? own : (party == 2 ? neutral : enemy)). Slot 2 has its own branch at 00806721 and never produces `enemy`. Membership in the three class arrays depends on nothing but party. (d) Detection then decides which list is PUBLISHED. Each 1Ch-byte entry record carries a level at +0Ch, created 2 for own and 0 otherwise (00804E70's second argument). 00806840 runs the sensor pass over the enemy and neutral arrays and writes +0Ch from the target's own accumulator at unit+1E8h+party*34h. The drain at 00807644/008077C2 keeps level 2 in the relation triple, copies level 1 into the `unknown` triple and drops level 0. The own triple is never drained. The level comes from a float in [0, 1.0] (00D7A24C) thresholded at 0.25 (00CE3868) and 0.5 (00CE3800) by 00805AF0. The sensor test 008048A0 is a horizontal-distance-and-bearing table lookup: distSq is (dx*dx + dz*dz) from the two world frames' +FCh and +104h with no height term, normalised by env*env*signature*tuning74*tuning74, with an extra tuning78*tuning78 factor for a submerged MSubmarine, matched against a per-(observerCategory, targetCategory) row of 1Ch-byte entries that carry a max normalised squared range, a mask bit, an optional bearing window and a per-second gain with a cap. Only own-triple units that are IsKindOf(05h) act as observers.

answer.question: (2) The slot layout as a producer-backed table.
answer.result: 0x12A0 bytes. Beyond what docs/FIXED_STEP_COUNTDOWN.md already had: +24h the contents-changed flag (set 00806818, cleared 008073E6 and 0080799C), +2Ch the time of this rebuild and +30h the seconds since the last one (008073C1..008073E1, read at 008068CD as the sensor dt), the five {count, head, tail} triples at +DD8h own, +DE4h enemy (head +DE8h), +DF0h neutral, +DFCh unknown and +E08h their union, and a FOURTH 61h-entry array of 0Ch-byte lists at +E14h, the per-class carry-over lists. 0xE14 + 0x61*0x0C == 0x12A0 exactly and 00805300 destroys that array with the same helper triplet as the other three. The entry record is 1Ch: vptr 00D08E78, +4h the unit, +8h the refreshed category, +0Ch the level, +10h/+14h/+18h a member list used only by group records.

answer.question: (3) The rebuild's cadence.
answer.result: Four rebuild sites. 00807A08 inside the 3-second countdown 008079B0 rebuilds every present slot and publishes only the ones whose +25h is set. 004E059B in BSP_Game_LoadMissionScene rebuilds the active local player's slot right after creating all three with a 0..2 loop at 004E0537 and arming 00807A50. 004C9E82 in BSP_Game_ApplyInGameInterface and 007C631C in FUN_007C5F60 both rebuild the active local player's slot. Unit death does not rebuild: 00779B43 and 0077D2B6 only mark the contexts dirty with 00803BA0.

answer.question: (4) What 00806B10 publishes into the nineteen category tables, counts or lists.
answer.result: Neither. recon[index][relation][category] is a MAP keyed by the unit's decimal entity id as a string: 00805D90 builds it with itoa(unit->+174h, 10) through 006B8120 as the key and 00927BF0's unit Lua value as the value, settable at -3 (006B84D0). The four relations map to triples: enemy -> +DE4h, own -> +DD8h, neutral -> +DF0h, unknown -> +DFCh; the fifth triple at +E08h is never published. 00805D90 drops ten class ids outright (0Fh, 10h, 11h, 12h, 14h, 15h, 16h, 17h, 13h, 19h), so individual planes and land vehicles never reach the script and only their squadron and convoy aggregates stand for them; the category itself is unit->[+170h]->vtable[0]() with 13h meaning none. 00805D90's third argument, 0 for own and 1 for the rest, is never read.

answer.question: (5) What distinguishes recon[0], recon[1] and recon[2].
answer.result: The index is the party (side) index: 0 and 1 the two belligerents, 2 the neutral side, which is why 008065B0 treats party 2 specially and why slot 2 has no enemies. BSP_Game_LoadMissionScene creates exactly three with for(i=0;i<3;++i) 008053C0(i) at 004E0537. 009F5D3A passes a unit's +54h. 00806840 and 008048A0 index the unit's three-entry detection array at +1E8h with the observer's +54h while 008065B0 indexes the same array with the slot's +28h. 00779B26 and 0077D29C walk exactly three of those 34h records per unit.

corrections.was: 008073C0 coverage row 'partial: only the five 008042B0 clears at 008073D0..00807416 and the list-1-to-list-3 move at 00807634..008076E2 were read', with the follow-up packet unit_registry_five_lists asking what the five triples separate
corrections.is: answered and complete. The five triples are own (+DD8h), enemy (+DE4h), neutral (+DF0h), unknown (+DFCh) and the union of those four (+E08h); the 1-to-3 move is the detection drain that copies level-1 records into the unknown triple and removes anything below level 2 from the relation triple
corrections.evidence: the whole body 008073C0-008079A5 is read in docs/RECON_SLOT_LISTS.md section 3; 00806B10's four 00805D90 calls at 00806BE4, 00806C1A, 00806C50 and 00806C86 fix the names; 00807647 and 00807823 are the level compares. That doc's reading that 004C3CB0 walks triples 0, 1 and 3 and the HUD triple 4 is consistent and not superseded.
